%% Question bank chapter file - generated by bank_tools.py build (do not edit while the bank is still being built:
%% it is regenerated from the per-test data in Question Bank\data). Every question is one bankq block:
%%   \begin{bankq}[id=..., source={...}, paper=.., qno=.., type=..., subtopic={...}, answer={...}, answer_src=key|solved,
%%                 working={...}, difficulty=1-10, diff_parts={K S I C F}, diff_note={...},
%%                 group=<passage id or empty>, also_in={duplicate copies in other tests}]
%% difficulty = min(10, K+S+I+C+F-1): K concepts 1-3, S steps 1-4, I insight 0-2, C computation 0-2, F format 0-1
%%   ...question LaTeX, options, figures (\bfig / \bfigi -> img/)...
%%   \end{bankq}
%% Passages shared by several questions are bankpassage blocks; their questions carry group=<passage id>.
\documentclass[10pt]{article}
\usepackage[a4paper,margin=1.8cm]{geometry}
\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb,mathtools}
\usepackage{graphicx}
\usepackage[export]{adjustbox}
\usepackage{xcolor,needspace,keyval}
\usepackage{enumitem}
\usepackage{booktabs,array,tabularx}
\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
\setlength{\parindent}{0pt}
\setlength{\parskip}{3pt}
\makeatletter
\define@key{bq}{id}{\def\bq@id{#1}}\define@key{bq}{source}{\def\bq@src{#1}}\define@key{bq}{paper}{\def\bq@paper{#1}}
\define@key{bq}{qno}{\def\bq@qno{#1}}\define@key{bq}{type}{\def\bq@type{#1}}\define@key{bq}{subtopic}{\def\bq@sub{#1}}
\define@key{bq}{answer}{\def\bq@ans{#1}}\define@key{bq}{answer_src}{\def\bq@asrc{#1}}\define@key{bq}{working}{\def\bq@work{#1}}
\define@key{bq}{group}{\def\bq@group{#1}}\define@key{bq}{also_in}{\def\bq@also{#1}}
\define@key{bq}{difficulty}{\def\bq@diff{#1}}\define@key{bq}{diff_parts}{\def\bq@dparts{#1}}\define@key{bq}{diff_note}{\def\bq@dnote{#1}}
\newenvironment{bankq}[1][]{\def\bq@work{}\def\bq@also{}\def\bq@group{}\def\bq@diff{?}\def\bq@dparts{}\def\bq@dnote{}\setkeys{bq}{#1}%
  \par\needspace{4\baselineskip}\medskip\noindent{\small\textbf{\bq@id}\hfill\color{gray}[\bq@src, Paper \bq@paper, Q\bq@qno]
  \bq@type\ $\cdot$ \bq@sub\ $\cdot$ \textbf{D\bq@diff}}\par\nopagebreak\relax}
  {\par{\small\color{teal}Answer: \textbf{\bq@ans}\ifx\bq@work\@empty\else\ (solved: \bq@work)\fi
  \ifx\bq@also\@empty\else\par\color{gray}Also in: \bq@also\fi}\par}
\define@key{bp}{id}{\def\bp@id{#1}}\define@key{bp}{source}{\def\bp@src{#1}}\define@key{bp}{questions}{\def\bp@qs{#1}}
\newenvironment{bankpassage}[1][]{\setkeys{bp}{#1}\par\needspace{4\baselineskip}\bigskip\noindent
  {\small\textbf{Passage \bp@id}\hfill\color{gray}[\bp@src; questions \bp@qs]}\par\nopagebreak\relax\itshape}{\par}
\makeatother
\newcommand{\bfig}[2]{\par\smallskip{\centering\includegraphics[width=#1pt,max width=0.62\linewidth,max height=0.32\textheight]{img/#2}\par}\smallskip}
\newcommand{\bfigi}[2]{\includegraphics[width=#1pt,max width=\linewidth,max height=0.32\textheight,valign=c]{img/#2}}
\newcommand{\bmissing}[1]{\textit{[figure missing in the source conversion: \detokenize{#1}]}}
\newenvironment{qoptions}{\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.8em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=2pt,label={}]}{\end{itemize}}
\newcommand{\opt}[2]{\item[(#1)] #2}
\providecommand{\fwstart}{}\providecommand{\fwend}{}\providecommand{\qfullsplit}{}
\newcolumntype{L}[1]{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{#1}}
\newcolumntype{C}[1]{>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{#1}}
\newcolumntype{R}[1]{>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}p{#1}}
\providecommand{\sectionhdr}[1]{}\providecommand{\subsectionhdr}[1]{}

\section*{Score-I papers}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI12-P1-PHY-S2-Q02, source={Score-I - Test 12 (09 Mar 2022)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=numerical, subtopic={Bohr model}, answer={5.00}, answer_src=key, difficulty=2, diff_parts={K1 S1 I0 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: Bohr model energy levels | steps: E = 13.6 Z^2 (1/4 - 1/9) = 47.2 gives Z}]
A single electron orbits a stationary nucleus of charge $+Ze$, where $Z$ is a constant and $e$ is the magnitude of the electronic charge. It requires 47.2 eV to excite the electron from the second Bohr orbit to third Bohr orbit. Find the value of $Z$.
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI12-P1-PHY-S2-Q03, source={Score-I - Test 12 (09 Mar 2022)}, paper=1, qno=3, type=numerical, subtopic={Nuclear physics}, answer={4.00}, answer_src=key, difficulty=2, diff_parts={K1 S1 I0 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: binding energy per nucleon curve | steps: read BE per nucleon for D, Li and He; Q = BE(products) - BE(reactants) and express in 5.5 MeV}]
The positions of ${}^2_1$D, ${}^4_2$He and ${}^7_3$Li are shown on the binding energy per nucleon curve as shown in figure. Find the energy released in the fusion reaction, ${}^2_1\text{D}+{}^7_3\text{Li}\to2\,{}^4_2\text{He}+{}^1_0\text{n}$ in multiple of 5.5 MeV.
\bfig{187.3}{SI12_p1_phy_s2_q03_1.png}
\end{bankq}
